The most natural way to use JackMoebius is the **[JackMate](https://zinc75.github.io/JackMate)**
GUI — a free, standalone JACK patchbay and manager, and the visual way to drive it: one box per
exposed app, per-app **Output / Input**, per-app volumes, live routing-status alerts, and
**studios** that save and restore your whole setup in one click. JackMate detects the installed
JackMoebius daemon automatically, with no path to configure.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## <i class="fa-solid fa-up-right-from-square"></i> See it all in JackMate

JackMate's own guide walks through every JackMate ↔ JackMoebius interaction — exposing apps,
per-app Output / Input and channel counts, per-app volumes, the wrong-device routing alerts,
and studios that restore your whole setup.

[**Open the JackMate guide to JackMoebius →**](https://zinc75.github.io/JackMate/guide/jackmoebius.html)
:::

JackMate is the **reference** front-end — but it isn't the only way in:

- **Any JACK patchbay or tool** — JackMoebius is driven entirely through a documented
  **[IPC protocol](ipc.qmd)** over a local socket. Nothing about it is JackMate-specific, so
  other developers are free to build JackMoebius support into their own tools.
- **The command line** — the `jackmoebius` CLI does everything the daemon can (see the
  **[CLI reference](cli.qmd)**): script it, automate it, or run it headless with no GUI at all.
